title: Specialized launches S-Works Diverge 4 gravel bike with internal cabling and 8.2kg claimed weight
content:
Cyclist
Specialized launches S-Works Diverge 4 gravel bike with internal cabling and 8.2kg claimed weight

Specialized has launched an S-Works version of its Diverge 4 gravel bike, which it says shaves 200g off the standard frame weight. It’s added almost-internal cable routing to clean up the front end while retaining its Future Shock fork with 20mm travel.   

Unlike other Diverges, which use the Fact 9r carbon layup, the S-Works Diverge is built on the same Fact 12r carbon fibre as used for the S-Works Tarmac SL9, reducing the frame weight by a claimed 200g to 950g for a painted size 56 frame. 

It also has semi-internal cabling at the front end, a first for a Future Shock-equipped bike. Previous iterations of Future Shock used both on the Diverge and the Roubaix SL8 have necessitated external cables at the front, due to the suspension mechanism. But the S-Works Diverge 4 has a new Future Shock 3.3 system, in which Specialized has routed the cables/hoses into the headset topcap, with a short external run, cleaning up the bike’s front end.

As usual with S-Works bikes, Specialized has bolted premium components to the S-Works Diverge, in its case a SRAM Red XPLR AXS groupset and Roval Terra CLX III wheels. There’s a Roval Terra one-piece cockpit and CeramicSpeed headset and bottom bracket bearings.

Rear compliance is delivered by the Diverge 4’s Roval Terra Carbon seatpost, which has a 20mm offset and is designed to deflect rearwards by up to 18mm. Roval says that it weighs under 200g and helps deliver rear wheel traction.

Other spec details are similar to the non-S-Works bikes. Tyre clearance is 50mm with 7mm of clear air all round. That’s not groundbreaking – the Crux 2 gravel race bike has 55mm tyre clearance – but it still allows you to fit reasonably wide tyres with adequate space for mud and debris. Specialized says that in addition to its 50mm Terra tyre, you can also opt for the 2.2in AirTrak XC MTB tyre, although clearance around the tyre then drops to 4mm.

The frame is 1x and 2x compatible and Specialized says you can fit a 46t max 1x chainring or 48/31t Shimano GRX or 43/30t SRAM Wide 2x chainring set. It reckons you can go as large as 52t – at your own risk.

The S-Works Diverge 4 has an 8.2kg claimed weight and will sell for £11,999 / $12,500 / €13,999.
